title: Other film shorts: Movietone, Universal, Columbia and Snader
summary: Barnet identifies shorts from 1947-51, recognizing Neal Hefti, Bud Shank and the California band in a still, and what company made each.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And here we have an 11 minute, Charlie Barnet and his Band, 1949, and the Director was Charles Skinner, the man you made the long movie for. It was one of Movietone Melody's series in which Charlie Barnet and His Band entertain with special arrangements of popular numbers, "Redskin Rhumba," "Atlantic Jump," and, "My Old Flame." Do you remember that?
Yeah. Was that done in New York?
It doesn't say. It's 1949, and Charles Skinner.
I think that was done in New York, at 20th Century studios.

Here's a picture of you and the band, but it doesn't say which of the films it's from. I'll show you in a second. The next one, Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, 14 minutes, Will Cowan, 1947, a Universal-International Featurette with Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, supported by singers Rita Shore and Della Norell, with Jeanne Blanche and dancers Igor and Tanía. Shorty Rogers, trumpet, Barney Kessel, guitar, are prominent in the final number. Music includes, "I Remember April," "No Can Do," "You're a Sweetheart," "Rhumba Fantasy," "I Believe in Miracles," and, "Murder at Payton Hall."
You mean we did one without, 'Skyliner'?
I guess you did. And I bet you this picture is from that one, because it looks like one of those sets. Is it?

No. There's a blond young lady in front of the band there. This -- Harry Babasin on bass. It's very difficult to tell. This looks like -- let me get just a little more light on the subject here, and we'll see what we've got here.
There's more films listed. I haven't mentioned these two yet.

Uh-huh. Oh, there's Neal Hefti on trumpet there, in this picture. Yeah, this was -- this was around that time, but I can't tell who the girl singer is there. I presume she's a singer. She's standing in front of the band. Although she's obviously not singing in that pose, but -- that's -- oh, yeah, Irving Lewis, trumpet. Yes, I recall this. This was around '47, '48. That was the California Band.
Okay. It has a California kind of looking set.
Neal Hefti was writing for it and also played in the trumpet section for awhile.
Yeah, I see Neal there, on the far right.
Yeah.
Uh-huh. That's Harry Babasin?
No, it isn't Harry Babasin. I think it's Red -- oh, he played with Red Norvo after that. Red -- I can't think of his name.
Did Bud Shank ever work for you?
Oh, yes.
That looks like Bud Shank in the saxophone section.
Yeah, it probably is him. Bud worked for me several times, as a tenor man and an alto man, both.

He's sure good. Okay. Then there's Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, 1948, 11 minutes, one of the Thrills of Music Series, featuring the orchestra in a program of music which includes, "Pompton Turnpike," "Stormy Weather," and "Civilization." It doesn't say for whom.
No, that was for Columbia, I think. I think that was done in New York.
And the next one is Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra in 1951, 18 minutes, Snader Telescription, featuring the title orchestra. That's all the information on that one.
Oh, I presume that was a group of those three minute wonders put together.
Six three minute wonders.
Yeah.

Okay. And then, "Cherokee," 1951, three minutes. Snader Telescription in which the title number is played by Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, including Claude Williamson, piano, Bill Holman, tenor sax, Dave Wells, trombone, and Bob Daws, baritone sax.
Yeah.
